observation: 100% test-first discipline — 110 tests written in red phase, all passed on first green-phase run. Zero test-driven rework cycles. Highest test-first success rate in pipeline (prior workpackages had 0-1 rework rounds due to schema drift, timeouts, or missing tests).

Plan prediction accuracy 100% — architecture plan specified 18 ACs, implementation delivered exactly 18. Zero unplanned scope creep, zero skipped ACs. Code review found zero 'MUST FIX' architecture deviations.
Concept phase completeness — all 7 design open questions resolved during concept without back-to-concept during architecture. Concept rejection list prevented scope creep on 3+ feature requests.

Architecture critique caught critical runtime bug (worker schema missing harnessType field) before code review. Prevented silent feature breakage for remote workers. Critique process highly effective.
Clean schema deprecation — soulPromptPath column preserved (not dropped), new soulPrompt column added. Rollback path exists. Zero data migration risk. Additive-only migration per architecture plan.
Security improvement documented — path traversal attack surface eliminated (no more filesystem reads of soul prompt content). Documented in @lore comment. Simpler threat model.
Comprehensive E2E coverage — 7 Playwright tests covering full user journey (render, edit, add, delete) with both happy-path and error-path scenarios. Tests use real API endpoints.

Critique-to-build integration weak — architecture critique identified 1 CRITICAL bug (worker schema) at 35ba3fea, but implementation at e8ea823b did not apply the fix. Bug re-discovered during code review (07c0ef32), then fixed in follow-up commit (a229de07). 3rd workpackage in a row where critique findings are re-discovered during code review instead of being proactively applied.

React Fragment key warning — SettingsAgents.tsx line 273-274 uses shorthand Fragment (<>) in .map() without key. Key placed on inner <tr>, not outer Fragment. Produces React lint warning. Caught during code review but not fixed during red/green phases.

Race condition in template pre-fill — rapid role changes in add form fire multiple async template fetches without abort controller or sequence counter. Stale fetch could show wrong template. Architecture critique flagged this as WARNING; implementation did not mitigate (no AbortController added). Accepted residual risk.

Design spec details skipped — implementation missing badge classes, textarea rows, gap spacing, font-mono placement. Functional ACs all pass, but visual polish 85-90% of spec. Builder optimized for AC binary pass/fail; designer optimized for visual fidelity. Mismatch at UI/design boundary.

Duplicate constants in web package — SettingsAgents.tsx redeclares USER_ROLES and MODEL_TIERS locally, duplicating constants from @hyperidle/shared. Drift risk if roles/tiers change. Caught by code review as SUGGESTION to consolidate imports.

Single-day workpackage feasibility — 18 ACs, 6565 lines delivered in ~16.5 hours wall-clock. Productive commits 92%, orchestration 8%. Throughput: ~55 min/AC. Feasible when scope is 15-20 ACs, spec is clear, builder is domain-familiar.

observation: Plan reconciliation table (architecture Section 0) caught 3 CRITICAL data model mismatches before code was written. Schema reality check proved invaluable. This should be a standard architecture pattern.

Critique findings (3 CRITICAL, 6 WARNING) fixed correctly on first implementation pass. No rework cycle. Suggests architecture plan was sufficiently detailed and builder internalized spec before coding.

Judge factory library (10 reusable judges) reduced duplicated code by ~120 lines per scenario. Extraction paid for itself immediately. Factories are simple, well-named, enable rapid scenario addition.

Seven scenario files use module-level `let` variables to pass state from seed() to judges. Creates latent reentrancy hazard if runner ever executes same scenario twice in one process. Currently safe (serial runner) but fragile pattern. Should extend ScenarioSeedResult with metadata bag.

LLM-as-judge usage minimal (2 of 60 dimensions). Those using LLM checks rely on heuristic keyword matching in session notes, which is fragile. Spec promised LLM reasoning but implementation is keyword-based. Inconsistency between intent and delivery.

Scenario registry (index.ts) has feature-based comments but alphabetically-sorted exports. Comments describe features but don't match export positions, creating maintenance debt. Either group by feature or remove comments entirely.

observation: Builder made 2 factual errors in gap audit: claimed retro auto-fire and cost sentinel were not implemented, but both ARE wired into the event dispatcher/scheduler. Root cause: builder verified service code existence but didn't trace registration into the runtime scheduler. Layer-spanning verification needs a reconciliation table.

Validation scenarios (facilitator routines, User Sovereignty) were not addressed in first draft. Reviewer caught them. Audit workpackages need validation scenarios as mandatory content gates in the concept phase, not just structural ACs.

Two review cycles required for audit doc (6 findings in Round 1, all fixed in Round 2). Matches Z2 pattern: documentation workpackages consistently need 2 review passes. Feature workpackages with tests sometimes pass in 1.

Research/audit throughput (~870 words/hour) is ~3.7x faster than narrative throughput (~233 words/hour from Z1). Different workpackage types have different cost profiles. Pipeline scheduling should account for this.

Pipeline correctly skipped /design, /architecture, /design-critique, /architecture-critique for a pure-research audit workpackage. The concept phase was a lightweight no-op (no new nouns). This is the right adaptation for doc/audit work.

TDD discipline + architecture critique = predictable delivery. 23 tests written in red phase, all passing on first implementation run. Architecture critique (8/10) resolved 7 spec-vs-reality items upfront. Zero mid-stream rework, only polish findings in code review. Pattern matches R5, S2, U4, X3.

CRITICAL-1: Nested button (invalid HTML) blocked code review R1. Design spec assumed interactive wrapping was possible, but HTML does not allow nesting. Architecture plan did not work through the HTML structure explicitly.

CRITICAL-2: Dialog stories crash in design system viewer because useToast() requires ToastRegion context which does not exist at /designsystem route. Context provider dependencies not specified in architecture plan.

Five warnings accumulated: always-mounted dialog (mock cascade), missing agentCategory in test fixture, no AbortController on template fetch (race condition), missing motion token, hint style inconsistency. Individually acceptable, collectively indicate rough edges.

Dual-review model (critique + code review) necessary for UI workpackages. Phase 2 critique caught structural gaps (nested button, story context). Phase 4 code review caught implementation details (defensive patterns, test fixtures). Neither alone would catch both CRITICALs.

Spec-vs-reality reconciliation (standard in AB3 architecture plan) eliminated build surprises. Tag variants, Avatar sizes, type extensions, endpoint filtering — all resolved upfront. Pattern observed in 12+ workpackages; should be mandatory architecture template section.

Always-mounted edit dialog forced useToast mock to cascade across 3+ test files (WorkProduct, hints, artifact-section). Fix: conditional mount (only when editingAgentId !== null) isolated the mock. Pattern recurs in component lifecycle design — prefer lazy mounting over hidden-state display.

Timeline: ~18 hours across 5 calendar days (non-continuous). Productive work: 16h (design, architecture, tests, code, review, retro). Infrastructure overhead: 2h (CI/attestation). Productive ratio: 89%. Review rounds: 2 (NOT DONE → fix → DONE). Cost acceptable for feature complexity (6 ACs, 2 new components, 1 hook).
